themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints exploded to 5 this week versus 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (3900% spike, z-score 14.74), suggesting rapid deterioration of sidewalk seating infrastructure or enforcement issues coinciding with spring restaurant openings (Prince Street Pizza Carroll Gardens outpost launching April 23).
evidence: 5 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3900% increase)
Z-score of 14.74 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Prince Street Pizza opening Carroll Gardens location April 23; Goop ghost kitchen arrival (April 17) signals restaurant expansion wave
Timing aligns with warm weather season onset and post-COVID outdoor dining normalization
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept. and SLA about outdoor dining permit surge and enforcement readiness as new restaurants launch
Document specific sidewalk obstruction complaints: are café chairs blocking accessibility, fire hydrants, ADA compliance?
Profile incoming restaurants and their outdoor dining plans—are they prepared for neighborhood capacity limits?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge in Park Slope
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 7 this week versus 1.5 weekly average (367% spike, z-score 4.49), marking the sharpest homelessness-visible crisis this week and aligning with repeated community board budget requests for homeless services funding.
evidence: 7 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (367% increase)
Z-score of 4.49 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Community Board budget requests (recurring, year-over-year) for Department of Homeless Services funding—unmet need signal
No recent DHS outreach or shelter capacity announcements for this district in available data
reporting_angles: Locate encampments and conduct welfare checks: who is unhoused, why, and what services are available?
Interview DHS and local nonprofits about spring surge and shelter bed availability in CD 306
Investigate gap between community board funding requests and actual DHS resource allocation to Park Slope/Carroll Gardens

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Mass Die-Off
themes_detail.summary: Tree mortality complaints surged to 9 this week versus 1.0 weekly average (800% spike, z-score 7.16), suggesting environmental stress, disease outbreak, or storm damage across the district this week that warrants urgent arboricultural investigation.
evidence: 9 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (800% increase)
Z-score of 7.16 indicates extreme statistical departure
Community Board repeatedly requests park reconstruction/upgrade and tree maintenance funding (unsolved chronic issue)
Overlaps with 'Damaged Tree' complaints (327 in 90-day period, steady baseline—suggests new acute event driving spike)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks forestry team: is this a pest outbreak, disease (e.g., ash borers), or weather-related (late frost, salt damage)?
Map the 9 complaints geographically—are dead trees clustered in one area or distributed across CD 306?
Investigate Parks Dept. response time and tree removal/replacement capacity given chronic underfunding requests

themes_detail.label: Maintenance Backlog Spike
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance and facility complaints jumped to 20 this week versus 5.9 weekly average (240% spike, z-score 4.62), indicating building/infrastructure repair requests are outpacing city response capacity this week across parks, schools, or municipal facilities.
evidence: 20 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (240% increase)
Z-score of 4.62 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Community Board budget requests for senior center renovation and park facility upgrades (chronic unmet need)
1,227 DOB building permits filed in 90 days (743 alterations pending—potential contractor/permit processing bottleneck)
reporting_angles: Request Parks Dept. and DCAS data on maintenance ticket backlog and typical response times
Interview facility managers at parks, senior centers, and schools about what is broken and unfixed
Investigate whether permit processing delays (DOB alteration queue) are cascading into deferred maintenance complaints

themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs Safety Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 5 three weeks ago versus 0.6 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 6.29), representing a lingering public safety hazard from deteriorated street furniture that may require urgent replacement before pedestrian injury.
evidence: 5 dangling street sign complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase)
Z-score of 6.29 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No follow-up resolution data provided—signs may still be hazardous
Overlaps with broader 'Street Condition' complaints (531 in 90-day period)
reporting_angles: Conduct visual audit of Park Slope/Carroll Gardens streets: document still-dangling signs and photograph safety risk
File FOIL request for NYC Department of Transportation sign repair work orders filed and completed for CD 306 in past 30 days
Interview residents and business owners about near-misses or injuries from falling street furniture
